trigger: Siege night 3 (the push). Never more than 3 visible. They break off at dawn or after losing 2.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Night three. No moon. Snow falling straight down. The lamp line hums.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: They come at one side only, the dark side behind the cooling towers. Fewer than you feared. More than you'd like.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: They come at two sides at once, testing which one breaks first. They're not a horde. They don't need to be.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: No dog to tell you where. You watch the lights instead: whichever one flickers first.

nodes.speaker: wraith
nodes.text: [Barking at the east fence. Then the north. Showing you where. Over and over.]

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Between the lamps, voices. Halvorsen's. Lolo's. Yours, calling for Wraith. Nobody answers. That's the rule.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: [On the radio] North pole four's dark! East three flickering! Braith, which one?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You get the light back on as a long shape steps into it. It flinches. It stops. It turns its flat eyes on you.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You hold the east with rifles. The north goes dark for ninety seconds. Long enough. Someone screams in the yard.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By dawn, two of them are dead in the snow outside the fence. The rest are gone. You don't know how many the rest is.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You stand at the fence with the sun coming up brown. The lamp line holds. For tonight. That's what holding means now.
